gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Furbo's own US store sells the $35 Furbo Mini 360° only together with a Nanny plan billed $83.92, so the cart total is $118.92, which is over $100, and that this purchase has a 3-month minimum during which Furbo 'reserve[s] the right to block their access to the service', while a Subscription-Required Furbo 'locks the live view' until a plan is linked.
standout_why: I compared five pages. TheConsumers.guide (cited) gives Wi-Fi bands (Furbo 360 and Bites 2 Lite are 2.4 GHz only, TKENPRO is dual-band) and a general treat size of 7–15 mm. HomeGearLab (cited) gives treat sizes for Furbo and Petcube and says the Furbo is '$35 with a Furbo Nanny plan' and needs a plan activated. VettedFur (cited) has the Petcube container and Wi-Fi band, but says 'Check each maker's page' for treat size. ChatGPT's answers show the Mini 360° at '$30–$49 promotional pricing' as if it fit under $100. None of these pages gives Furbo's checkout total of $118.92, the Standard plan billed at $83.92, the 3-month minimum from Furbo's own terms, the live-view lock on Subscription-Required units, or the $2/month charge for each extra camera. I couldn't open WIRED (fetch blocked) or PawCog (SSL error).
decides: This confirms Petcube Bites 2 Lite ($99.99 at petcube.com) as the pick. It's the only maker-sold treat camera here where the free tier 'Comes with every Petcube camera' with live streaming and the total stays under $100. The Furbo Mini 360° bought at its $35 price on furbo.com costs $118.92 at checkout, so it should be listed as over budget or as a plan bundle, not as a $30–49 under-$100 option. Petcube's Optimal yearly Care plan is now $4.99/mo ($59.88/yr), so our page's 'bundles from $5.99' should change.

findings.label: Price at checkout on furbo.com with the device at $35
findings.value: Device $35 (crossed-out $99) + Standard Nanny plan 'Billed at $83.92' = 'Add to cart - $118.92'
findings.note: $35 + $83.92 = $118.92, over the $100 budget. The page has a plan selector ('Choose your Furbo Nanny plan', Standard 'Avg. $6.99/mo' with $9.99 crossed out, 3-day video history). I saw no device-only option in the page text. The page header also says 'Sign up to unlock 60 days of FREE Furbo Nanny'.

findings.label: Treat capacity and voice assistant (maker comparison chart)
findings.value: 'Lite toss, up to 10 small treats'; Alexa: Yes; Google Assistant not listed; Nanny 'starting at $9.99/mo'
findings.note: The chart lists Furbo 360° Dog/Cat at 100-treat capacity. The Mini 360° holds about a tenth of that. The page doesn't say whether any model needs a subscription.

findings.label: Exclusion: live view locked until a plan is linked; extra-camera fee
findings.value: The setup prompt 'locks the live view' until a Nanny plan is activated and linked. On Subscription-Optional models, Live View, 2-way audio, treat tossing and basic alerts work without a plan. One plan covers one camera, with 'a $2 monthly fee' for each additional camera
findings.source_title: Why is my new Furbo asking for a subscription if I already have a Furbo Nanny plan – Furbo Help Center
findings.note: The article doesn't name which SKUs are Subscription-Required. It says the camera shows an activation prompt during setup.

findings.label: Minimum term and what still works after cancelling
findings.value: 'minimum subscription of three (3) continuous months'. Furbo 'reserve[s] the right to block their access to the service until they renew'. After cancelling, 'you will only be able to access a real-time stream'
findings.source_title: Subscription Services – Furbo Dog Nanny, 'Subscribe & Save' and Premium Safety Package Users – Furbo Help Center
findings.note: Blocking is a right Furbo reserves, not something that always happens. The terms also mention a 'Camera Only' purchase option, but I couldn't find its price on furbo.com.

findings.label: Cancellation and what stays free afterwards
findings.value: 'You can cancel anytime after your initial subscription period ends', after which 'you'll still have access to the basic features'
findings.source_title: How to Setup and Activate Camera (Subscription Required) – Furbo Help Center
findings.note: This covers 'Subscription Required Furbo from Amazon'. Units bought on furbo.com follow a different guide.

findings.label: Treats it accepts (maker help article)
findings.value: Dry, firm, round treats. The article says both 'about 0.5 inches (1 cm) in diameter' and '0.25 in (0.6 cm) to prevent jams', with 'at least 0.25 in diameter to stack properly'
findings.source_title: Best Treats for Furbo Mini 360 – Furbo Help Center
findings.note: The article contradicts itself on size. The safe range across both statements is 0.25–0.5 in (0.6–1 cm). It gives 1–2 treats per toss for most brands.

findings.label: Treats it accepts, Wi-Fi and phone requirements, price
findings.value: 'crunchy treats with dimensions of 1 inch or less, uniform in size and shape (ideally spherical)'; 3 inserts limit treats per fling; 'iOS 14 and higher or Android 7.1.2 and higher (supporting 2.4GHz WiFi)'; $99.99 (list $149.99)
findings.source_title: Petcube Bites 2 Lite Smart Pet Camera with Treat Dispenser
findings.note: It takes treats up to about 2.5 cm, roughly 2.5× the Furbo Mini 360°'s 1 cm maximum. The 1.5 lb container is dishwasher safe up to 130°F. In the box: USB cable, Petcube power adapter, mounting kit.

findings.label: Care plans and what's free
findings.value: Basic/Free 'Comes with every Petcube camera' with 'Live video streaming'; Optimal $4.99/mo yearly ($59.88) or $9.99/mo monthly; Premium $11.99/mo yearly ($143.88) or $16.99/mo, 'Unlimited cameras covered'
findings.note: The Care page doesn't say whether treat tossing and two-way audio work without Care. Our page's 'bundles from $5.99' is out of date: the yearly Optimal plan is $4.99/mo.

Furbo Mini 360° Wi-Fi band: neither the Furbo product page nor the comparison page states it. The '2.4GHz only' figure comes from TheConsumers.guide, not Furbo.
Furbo Mini 360° device-only price with no plan on furbo.com: the product page text shows only the plan selector.
Whether treat tossing (not just live view) is locked on Subscription-Required Furbo units before activation: Furbo's help article names only live view.

Which specific Furbo SKUs or listings are Subscription-Required in the US: the help articles don't name them, and Best Buy's 'subscription required, 3-month minimum' Mini 360 listing is Canadian (bestbuy.ca), which I didn't open.
Petcube Bites 2 Lite Alexa and Google Home compatibility: the maker page doesn't list either, and I didn't find a Petcube help article for it.
Geeni GN-WP pet treat feeder treat size, Wi-Fi band and app requirements: I didn't reach a maker page within the tool budget.
